M1.name: Separate native helper and monitor binaries
M1.topology: GUI Rust UI plus console keep-awake and monitor-helper binaries, still three processes.
M1.shared_code: One Cargo package with shared power and monitor modules and small entrypoints; not duplicate codebases.
M1.behavior: Reuse current separate Child handles, independent monitor, stdout/log format, ordinary forced Stop, and UI-crash child gap.
M1.ownership: Same parent-owned two Child handles, external monitor process handle, helper power handle, explicit partial cleanup, ordinary forced Stop, and UI-crash gap as M2. No Job Object.
M1.manual_console: Direct helper mode uses console control handling and visible output. GUI parent keeps child startup hidden.
M1.build_bootstrap: Native launcher is first built externally by Cargo or supplied as approved prebuilt output. Later same-release builds include all three runtime sibling outputs and exclude launcher.
M1.rollback: Port helper, monitor, launcher, then tools. Roll back each slice to the previous Python or accepted Rust slice.
M1.benefits: Closest process and observation semantics with separate failure boundaries.
M1.costs: Three runtime artifacts and sibling path wiring require one same-release build.
M1.unknowns: Native binding, control handler, readiness timeout, and launcher bootstrap are untested.
M1.tooling_phase: Port or explicitly retire every owned tool after runtime and launcher parity. Capture is archive or retire only.

M2.name: One Rust binary with explicit modes
M2.topology: One runtime binary serves UI, helper, and monitor modes, still three processes.
M2.shared_code: One Cargo package and one binary with common modules and mode dispatch before UI, log, or power side effects.
M2.behavior: Reuse the same separate Child handles, independent monitor, ordinary forced Stop, and UI-crash gap as M1; mode startup changes.
M2.ownership: Same parent-owned two Child handles, external monitor process handle, helper power handle, explicit partial cleanup, ordinary forced Stop, and UI-crash gap as M1. No Job Object.
M2.manual_console: Proposed untested route: console-subsystem runtime; native launcher starts UI hidden, owned modes hidden, and manual helper mode with terminal output and control handling. Direct UI invocation needs a decision.
M2.build_bootstrap: Native launcher is first built externally by Cargo or supplied as approved prebuilt output. Later builds target the runtime mode binary and exclude launcher.
M2.rollback: Port shared native code and modes one slice at a time. Roll back each mode slice to the previous Python or accepted Rust slice.
M2.benefits: Fewer runtime artifacts and no helper-image version mismatch while retaining three processes.
M2.costs: GUI and console behavior needs a real decision; one binary has more mode dispatch paths.
M2.unknowns: Direct invocation, hidden console behavior, control handling, readiness, and launcher bootstrap are untested.
M2.tooling_phase: Port or explicitly retire every owned tool after runtime and launcher parity. Capture is archive or retire only.

M3.name: One Rust process with internal modules
M3.topology: One process owns UI, power request, and monitor modules. No external helper or monitor observer.
M3.shared_code: One Cargo package with shared in-process modules.
M3.behavior: Changes process identity, pane meaning, startup coordination, cancellation, panic behavior, and liveness semantics.
M3.ownership: Owner process handles its own resources, but in-process cancellation and panic ownership need new rules. No Job Object.
M3.manual_console: Manual helper mode needs a replacement for current visible Ctrl+C behavior or an explicit scope decision.
M3.build_bootstrap: Native launcher is first built externally by Cargo or supplied as approved prebuilt output. Later builds target one runtime binary and exclude launcher.
M3.rollback: Port internal modules behind staged slices and retain the prior multi-process endpoint until each slice passes.
M3.benefits: Removes child startup and sibling path coordination.
M3.costs: Loses external observation and separate failure boundaries; changes cleanup and pane contracts.
M3.unknowns: In-process cancellation, panic cleanup, self-heartbeat meaning, and endpoint parity are untested.
M3.tooling_phase: Port or explicitly retire every owned tool after runtime and launcher parity. Capture is archive or retire only.
